Here too we have pictures of Mr. MacKinnon who has not been here for a long time and whom we have almost forgotten and also of Mr. Hughes the hon. member for King's whom we are pleased to see here with us all the time. These pictures are placed in the paper for the purpose of deceiving the people with regard to this work. These are both excellent young men; I have no objection to their appearance in the papers, and apart from their being young and fine looking they are jolly good fellows as well. But it is a serious matter and I find here in that very paper the proposition that a revote of $35,000 is to be taken in connection with the Summerside breakwater. I remember very well, as my hon. friend from East Prince (Mr. Lefurgey) has said, when he was running his election in 1898, that his opponents, on scores of platforms, said that Summerside harbour would be made one of the finest harbours in Prince Edward Island, and that the government were going to make a large grant for that purpose.
Is that what beat him, because he advocated this breakwater ?

There is no doubt it elected his opponent on that occasion. But I can tell you that afterwards at a local election, when Mr. Desroehes was running against Angus McMillan in Summerside, Mr. McMillan was elected by two votes, simply because he told the people of Summerside and that section of the country that if they supported him there would be a tremendous boom at Summerside and great works would be carried out. Yet for five years nothing has been done, and now we find that, on the eve of another election,, for the purpose of deceiving the people again, this amount is put in the estimates below the pictures of the two hon. gentlemen who care not one snap about Summerside.

If our hon. friends opposite are not in favour of this item, I would suggest that it be struck out. There are many places in the county I represent which would be glad to get this money, and where it could be usefully employed.

If this item is struck out, then the hon. gentleman opposite (Mr. Hughes) must take the responsibility of it.
New Brunswick-Black Brook - additional wharf accommodation, $5,000.
Perhaps the minister will give us some information with regard to this work.

This is asked for to afford wharf accommodation, which is urgently needed in the interest of a rapidly growing trade. A government wharf had been built, and an effort was made to acquire the land. The department and the owner of the property were widely apart as to the price. After some negotiations, a few months ago we came to a satisfactory arrangement, the papers have passed the Department of Justice, and the land is now the property of the Crown. This $5,000 is asked to make the settlement, and to make some addition to the wharf that has been acquired.

Are we to understand that the government built a wharf there on somebody else's property without acquiring it, and now they are paying the forfeit by asking this parliament to vote $5,000 to settle up for some of their mistakes ?
' The MINISTER OP PUBLIC WORKS. I am afraid that is about the state of affairs.
Cape Tormentine-improvements, $10,000.
What improvements is it proposed to make at Cape Tormentine ?

This is a large and important place, as my hon. friend knows. This vote is asked principally for stone work. I Understand that the structure is in a bad state of repair, and unless something is done immediately great damage is likely to be done to this important work.
Is a new pier to be built outside ?
This is for a terrace alongside the present work.
Are they going to extend the wharf V

Not under this vote. This is only for protection to the present work.
Campobello-breakwater at Wilson's beach (revote), $3,000.
Perhaps the minister would tell us how much this work has already cost ?
In round figures $30,000.
Is this $3,000 presumed to finish it ?
Yes.
How far has the work proceeded already ? Can any one get near it with a vessel ?

The work at present is 207 feet long, and

when the additional work is done it will be 455 feet long. I do not see that I have any ref erence, to the depth-of the water.

This is one of the votes that we had some talk of before. Some hon. members might think that it is unwise in me to criticise it because it refers to my county. But, I will criticise it very freely because I think if this system were followed throughout the country instead of having a vote of $67,000,000 we would require a vote of $367,000,000 to meet the requirements of the country. Instead of letting this work by tender so as to give the fishermen of that district value for every dollar that is expended the government have undertaken to do the work themselves and we have got about $20,000 worth of work for an expenditure of $30,000. Nineteen tiers have been put where there is a 30 foot rise and fall of the tide and yet after two year's work a vessel cannot approach the work. The total excess expenditure there of $10,000 has been used simply to furnish some work for good supporters of the present government.

I have no information except what I have read from the report of the engineer. My hon. friend is a very shrewd business man. I am informed that the department have advertised for tenders and that they have not received one either from the hon. gentleman or any of his constituents offering to do this work. Therefore, I suppose they would have to do it under the supervision of the engineer.

There was not much effort made in that direction. However, as we have discussed it before it is useless to waste the time-of the committee.
Campbellton-wharf extension, repairs, &c.,
Was there not some grant made in the main estimates for this same purpose 7

Yes, we have $15,000 in the main estimates. This is to extend the present wharf at Campbellton a distance of 300 feet. This additional vote includes the payment, when the sum is known, to Mr. Shive, for the property which was purchased from him.
Is this another instance in which the government are building a wharf without obtaining the property from Mr. Shive 7

No, I do not think this is a similar case. It was not necessary to purchase the whole property. Expropriation proceedings were taken, the property has been taken over and vested in the crown but the settlement has not been made. The amount in the estimates will pay for the property when the
award is made and it will carry out the improvements proposed.
Is this all a new work 7
The total probable cost of this work is $35,000.

That is not just the point I was after. This appears to be an extension simply of the wharf. There must have been an original wharf to be able to extend it. Was the title to the original wharf vested in the government 7 Do they own the property 7
I understand that the crown do own the property upon which the new wharf has been built. They had not a title to the adjoining property which has since been taken over by expropriation.
Why do the government want this additional property if they had the property on which to build the wharf 7

I understand that there is quite a large amount of shipping done at this point. It was necessary to acquire this in the public interest and it was very much cheaper than to have extended our own property.
What I understand by the extension of a new work is that you extend it out into the ocean. Why do you want more land 7

It is not so in this case, and we are not requiring any more land at all. There was a wharf built alongside the government wharf but it was found insufficient for the trade of the place. Being alongside of the government wharf it was purchased and united with the government wharf so as to make one large wharf to furnish the necessary facilities for this port.
Why does the wharf want to be so wide that you should buy more land 7	_
We are not buying more land.
If you are expropriating what are you expropriating 7
Part of this wharf may be on a water lot. The wharf was acquired and the land with it.
You have bought a wharf and then you have extended it.
It was built years ago.

We don't want to go back into ancient history. We are talking about what we are doing now.

Chatham-slip for lightship, $5,000.

This work was undertaken on the representations of the Department of Marine and Fisheries. It was represented that it would effect a large saving to the country if lightships could be taken in there, repaired and then taken out early in the spring.
Cocagne-wharf, compensation to Captain Antoine Arsenault of the schooner ' Morning Star ' for damages to his vessel resulting from the failure of a defective mooring post, $250.
What is the explanation of this item ?
Who owns the schooner 1

; This is for damage done to a schooner owned by Captain Antoine Arsenault. This vote is asked for on the report of the officials of the department. I have no doubt it is a fair settlement of the damage.
Do the government take the position that they are liable for all these troubles ? They might become liable for a buoy getting displaced ?

I am not lawyer enough to tell my'hon. friend how he will collect any claim against the government, but I always have taken the stand that if the government representing the country is responsible for anything it should be in very much the same position as any honest man would be. It should settle any claim that is a proper one V
How could the captain of this vessel have any claim against the government ?
He claimed that on account of some negligence in connection with the government works this schooner was damaged. The claim was for $500 but it was compromised at $250 by the officials.
Where was the mooring post ?
At Cocagne.

Occasionally vessels have got into trouble in the locks and mooring posts have given way but in every case the government have claimed this was the fault of the vessel because of too heavy a strain being put on the post. This now forms a precedent for other vessels in the case of accidents of this kind happening in the canals. This establishes a tery serious precedent for the future.
I do not think so.
This has the appearance of having a friend at court, and the country will view it in that light.
The precedent now established by the minister renders the government liable to this sort of damages for all time to come.

It is an exaggeration to say that it will be a precedent. I do not see why the government should not be liable for damages the same as any one else. I have no personal knowledge of this ; it was referred to the officials and they reported in favour of paying it.

I agree with the minister that when the government causes damage they should be responsible, but as I understand it, such a case as this should be referred to the Exchequer Court. Has this matter been referred to the Department of Justice for an opinion, or why did it not go to the Exchequer Court ?

This is a small matter, and the hon. gentleman knows that it would be cold justice to ask the claimant to go to the courts. I do not think he would have much left by the time he got his $250 damages. I have confidence in the officers of the department to which this matter was referred, and I believe they must have been satisfied that there was a just claim for this amount.

If a private individual owned a wharf and if a vessel came up to it to load or unload, does the minister think (hat if a storm came and the vessel sustained damage, the private individual would be liable ?

I am not a lawyer, but if the hon. gentleman asks me what would be fair between man and man, I would say that if the owner of the boat paid his fee-and I have heard complaints that the wharfage fees are pretty high on the lakes-and if the mooring posts were not sufficient, I imagine that the owner of the wharf would be liable. However, I do not care to offer an opinion on that.
What revenue is derived from this wharf or is it a free wharf ?
I understand it is a free wharf.
Then we give this man the use of the wharf, free, and pay him for tearing it to pieces.

I am not objecting to the amount of this vote, but I object to paying this amount when you compel other people to go to the Exchequer Court for claims just as small. If there is a dispute about expropriation it has to go to the 'Exchequer Court.
That is in a case where the officers will not recommend paj^ment.

I object to this because it forms a precedent to which the government is bound for all time.
THE MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS. Oh, no.
I certainly think it will.	'
Here is a ease) in which the wharf is given free of charge, and if a man ties his vessel up to it, and takes all the advantages of that wharf free of charge, you pay him if he sustains any damage.

There are many cases of this kind in which the government has not paid damages. Suppose a vessel is loaded with a valuable cargo, and that the cargo is damaged, would not the government on the same principle be liable for a large amount to compensate for the cargo ? I am afraid that the government has done an unwise thing in establishing this precedent.
Dalhousie harbour-improvements, $10,000.
THE MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS. This is to make improvements at this wharf so that ships may receive cargoes of lumber direct, without the necessity of using lighters.
What will be the total cost of this work ?
The probable total cost is estimated by the engineer at $40,000.
Is this the first amount that, has been voted ?

Yes.
Dipper harbour-breakwater, $10,000.

This is asked by the chief engineer to make provision for the construction of a protection breakwater 235 feet long, 44 feet wide on top, and reaching to a depth of 32| feet high water in spring tide. The new work is to be built on the site occupied by the old pier on the western side of the harbour. The foundation of the new breakwater has already been partly prepared, and the work is to be done by contract. Its total cost is estimated to be $25,000.
Was any money expended at this point last year ?

I am informed that there was not.
Hopewell Cape wharf-repairs, &c., $5,800.
This is to complete the work under contract. The amount of the contract is $19,998.
When was this contract let ?
On the 8th of October, 1900, to be completed on the 8th of October, 1901.
Was it completed ?

No, it has only been completed recently.
Miseou harbour-wharf, $5,000.
Is this a new wharf, and will this complete ?
This is a new work, and this vote is to commence it. The total estimated cost is $11,850.
What county is it in 7
Gloucester county.
Is there any village at the place, and what object is to be served by the construction of the dock ?

It is an island on which there are about seventy houses and eleven lobster factories. The population is estimated at about 500. The occupation of the people is mostly fishing. Farming is carried on to some extent.
And is the government going to build a $11,000 dock on an island where there are only 500 people ? Does anybody contribute anything towards the cost of the dock ?
As there are eleven lobster factories, there must be considerable commerce.

If the trade, is sufficient to warrant the construction of a dock, why do not the people in the business construct it ?
North Head breakwater wharf, Grand Manan, $10,000.
Perhaps the minister will advise us as to how large a work he purposes at Grand Manan ?

This is a pretty extensive work. The total cost, as estimated by the engineer of the department is about $91,000.
Petit Rocher-breakwater, $6,000.
Is this a new work ?
Yes, this is a new work. This vote is to make provision for the construction of a breakwater 350 feet long. The total cost is estimated at $27,400.
What county is this in ?

Gloucester county.

Pointe du Ch6ne-repairs to breakwaters, $4,000.

This vote is to make good damage "done to the works caused by a storm last January, and to protect other breakwaters with stone ballasting.
Richibucto harbour-extension oi north pier (revote), $3,000.
This is to pay the balance, of the contract, which completes the work.
May I ask if any report has been made as to the cost of dredging at St. Andrews ?

I may say that a report has been asked for, but has not yet reached the department.
Amherstburg, Ont.-dredging, $15,000.

This is rather an expensive and important work. It has been under discussion for some time. It is estimated that it can be carried out for $45,000, and I am asking for a vote of $15,000.
Mi-. HUGHES (Victoria). What is the general traffic at Amherstburg ?

There is a very large amount of shipping there, and considerable amount of difficulty is found on the Canadian side in competing with the Americans, who have spent a good deal on improvements on their harbours.
Has the government dredge been working there ?
No, this is for next season, and we intend trying to improve the facilities of the harbour.
There was an item voted last year, was it not expended ?

No, there were many difficulties about carrying on the work. We have adopted a plan by which I think we can, for the amount I have stated, do some good work for the harbour.
Blind river wharf-addition of head block, $3,000.
Is there any revenue at all from this dock? It is in the district of Algoma. I believe. What was the original cost of the dock ?
$9,310. The wharf has not been completed and handed over to the Marine Department yet, so that there is no revenue. I understand that the country is developing fast.
Where is this river ?
It is eighty miles east of Sault Ste. Marie.
Was there not money expended there last year ?

The contract was completed and the total cost was some $9,000.
Barry's Bay, Madawaska river-wharf, $1,500.

This is to provide for a small wharf there. There is a great increase in mining going on there and quite a settlement. After looking into the matter carefully, I found that a small wharf would be a great accommodation for that section and a great convenience for the shipping and mining industries.
What representations were made to the department by the citizens ?
A very important deputation, including the head of the mines there, waited on me; and on their representation, I looked into the matter and am satisfied that this is a very proper work.
Will this complete the work?
Yes.
How will this be expended?

By contract. I am letting the construction of all these small hew works by contract.
Bracebridge-wharf, $5,800.
Will that complete that work, and does it include the purchase of a site, and is the town contributing anything?
This is in new Muskoka. I do not see any estimate made for the site, so I take it for granted that it is not costing anything.
Will the $5,S00 complete the work ?
Yes.

It is a very necessary work. Bracebridge is an arm from Lake Muskoka. There is a-great deal of summer traffic there. The wharf was one of the promises given in the recent election. but for all that it is a very necessary work.
Bronte harbour-improvements, $6,300.
This is to complete the work going on.
Is that private property or do the government own it ?

Bronte harbour is in Halton county. I have not the information here, but it never oc-

curred to me that it was not public property. A very considerable amount of money has been spent there. Probably my hon, friend knows. I will look into the matter. It never occurred to me that it is not public property.
Burlington channel piers-to complete works of renewal and repairs under contract'(revote) $10,000.
This is on account of work going on.
Are these places to be found in the geography ?
It connects with Burlington Bay, and is the entrance to Hamilton at the bar.

We regard ourselves as the maritime part of the country, and we only get $313,000 for expenditure on harbours and rivers. But when we come to an inland country like Ontario, we find an expenditure of $142,000 more. I do not want to complain, because if every dollar is rightly asked, it is my duty to vote for the expenditure, whether it be in Ontario or Nova Scotia; but after hearing from the other side, during the past ten or twenty years, constant abuse for the voting of money to harbours in a really maritime province" like Nova Scotia, it seems a want of politeness for Ontario to get a half a million dollars for wharfs and harbours in a purely inland country. I merely want t.o bring that to the notice of gentlemen opposite from Ontario who spoke so vigorously about Nova Scotia votes. If these items are necessary, I will be glad to vote for them, but I hope that this talking about Nova Scotia or British Columbia votes, simply because these provinces are at the extremities of the Dominion, will cease. If they do not we will have to criticise items in Ontario. There must be absolute reciprocity in this matter. The only inquiry that should be made by members of this House is : Is it necessary and in the interests of Canada as a whole.

I quite agree with the hon. gentleman who has just taken his seat (Mr. Gourley) but I wish to call his attention, to the fact that we want to have the same rule applied to all the provinces. We have fishermen in Ontario. They are not along side the sea it is true, but they are beside waters that are asi important to us as the waters of any other province are to it. When we find fishermen in other districts of Canada having harbours provided for them out of public funds we think it is hardly fair that our fishermen, who have paid their license fees to this government and are now paying them to the Ontario government should be refused a small sum like $1,000 or $1,500 to make their harbours safe. We have then reason to complain and I do complain. The bon. gentleman states that in Nova Scotia
they have harbour votes of $314,000. Let me remind him that one of our large counties in Ontario is nearly as large as Nova Scotia.
I think that Nova Scotia is getting its share of harbour votes.
How many harbours have you ?

I suppose as many as you have in Nova Scotia. If Nova Scotia is getting this money and it is properly expended there I am glad to hear it and I trust that it will be properly expended, but when we look at that expenditure we in Ontario are justified in pointing out that many ports, such as are helped in Nova Scotia, are not helped in Ontario.

In connection with the vote for Burlington channel I wish to say a few words in answer to the hon. member for Nova Scotia who seems to think Ontario is getting more than its fair share. This is a work of great importance. Although it is called Burlington channel it is not in my county but it is very close to it ; it is the entrance to Hamilton from Lake Ontario. Vessels from Lake Ontario going into Hamilton harbour must pass' through this Burlington channel. In the early days this channel was nearer to the south shore, but perhaps seventy-five years ago the government closed up the old channel and made this new channel. I believe the work was first constructed about 1825. It has, however, become very much out of repair ; in fact I think the government is making a sad mistake in not appropriating somewhere about $250,000 and making one complete job of the whole thing. By spending $10,000 this year and $25,000 next year I am afraid that this work will never be put in proper shape.

This work was under contract just in the way that riiy hon. friend suggests and this extra amount of $10,000 is taken in the supplementary estimates in addition to $50,000 in that main estimate. This $10,000 is to be paid on account of the contract this year. The work is being carried on just in the way my hon. friend advises and I hope It will be completed early next season.

I am quite sure that the money that has been appropriated during the last two or three years is not sufficient for the requirements and it will be necessary for the government to spend very considerably more to keep that channel open. It is an absolute necessity not only for the city of Hamilton but for the entire country around there that has its shipping interests bound up with the important city of Hamilton, that the channel should be kept open.
Cumberland wharf, $5,500.

This is on the Ottawa river in Russell coup-

ty ; it is a new work and this is the estimate which the chief engineer thinks will complete the work.
How much has the municipality contributed to this ?
They have not contributed anything to it.
What is the population ?

I believe this is the only county on this river that has not one or more wharfs. The reeve called on me and I was perhaps a little weak, but I gave way. They have a large trade there. The place is about twenty miles from the city of Ottawa.
Has a site been procured ?

The site will be given free.
Collingwood-improvements to harbour, $60,000.
In a general way this is to continue work that has been going on there in winding the channel from 110 to 220 feet principally by dredging.

To what width is it intended to widen the channel with this vote and will this complete the work ? The chief engineer tells me that this vote will go a long way towards completing work. It will make a bell shaped entrance of 300 feet long for the whole channel, 20 feet at low water.
$60,000 will make it a width of 200 feet all the way down ?

That is the estimate of the engineer.
Depot Harbour-breakwater, $20,000.
I see by the main estimates there were $75,000 aud $25,000 more in subsequent estimates. Will the minister say what the total cost is likely to be, and how much has been spent already ?

The total cost is estimated in round figures at $195,000. In round figures about $00,000 has been spent, and $40,000 will complete the work.
Grand Bend-breakwater pier, &c., $5,000.
This is in the county of Lambton. A large deputation came to the department representing that this work was required, and that it would be a great convenience to a large population.
What amount does the hon. minister propose to expend there ?
If we carry out the plan as formed by the
engineer, the total work, bridge and all, will cost aibout $22,000.
What will be the depth of water ?

Twelve feet at low water. As soon as this vote is passed and the contract is let, the work will be commenced.
Goderich-breakwater off entrance to harbour, $20,000.	'

Representations have been made by the shipping interests that if a breakwater were built at Goderich that would become a first-class harbour. At present all the boats going up and down Lake Huron are forced to go to the American side when there is a storm, for want of a refuge. At present boats in a heavy sea have great difficulty in entering Goderich harbour. I was waited on personally by representatives of the shipping trade, who told me that if a breakwater was placed there it would be a great convenience and benefit to shipping. After consultation with the engineers, I came to the conclusion to make at first 200 feet as a trial, to see whether it would prove effectual and yield the benefits claimed by the representations made to me. This will only cost some $53,000. If it proves successful, we might extend the work. They asked for 1,700 feet, which would cost in' the neighbourhood of $200,000.
What would be the depth of that 1,700 feet ?
Twenty-five or thirty feet.
Would it not be cheaper to dig into the shore for your harbour V

This matter has been taken up, not alone by the Goderich people, but by the large business find commercial interests of Ontario, especially from Toronto west, who represent in the strongest manner the importance of this work. I am asking for this vote of $20,000 for the purpose of making a trial of 200 feet of this breakwater. If it proves as successful as these gentlemen have represented. I am sure it will be a work much in the interest of Canada.
What is the total expenditure on Goderich harbour up to date ?

This has nothing to do with the previous works. I know that a great deal of public money has been spent in Goderich on public works, but much of it, I fear has not been very useful for the want of this breakwater protection. I cannot at this moment give my hon. friend the amount expended by the Department of Public Works on the Goderich harbour. But this proposed work has nothing to do, except in an indirect way,

with any expenditure that has already been made on that harbour.
iMr. INGRAM. This is a serious question for the shipping interests in the town of Goderich. They have had breakwaters built there. I do not know whether they have 'been successful or not. Perhaps the hon. member for Huron (Mr. Holmes) could tell us where this breakwater is intended to be built.
Mr. HOLME'S. I may supplement the Information given by the Minister of Public Works. The chief object in making this breakwater is to make Godierich a harbour of refuge. There is no harbour! of refuge on the shores of Lake Huron within 150 miles. It was originally intended that Goderich should be a harbour of refuge, but that idea has never! been carried out. A number of lives have been lost during storms, simply because the vessels were unable to get in during a heavy sea. The purpose is to build a breakwater out into the lake 700 or 800 feet from the entrance of the harbour, whereby vessels could safely enter during a storm. No breakwater has paver been built in that direction, but only at the side of the river. Originally the piers ran in a south-westerly direction, but twenty-five or thirty years ago, at aj very great cost, the engineer ran the piers out straight, w-hie'h was a mistake, because they allowed the full force of the waves to come in. I may say also that the deputation which waited upon the hon. minister did not happen to be headed by the 'admiral,' as the hon. gentleman calls him. It happened to be headed by the mayor of Godierich, who is not a political supporter of my own. In addition to that, representations have been made to the government by the shipping men from all sections of the province of Ontario. A large quantity of grain has been handled at Goderich during the past year. They have ample water in the harbour for the largest lake-going vessels. and I believe that many vessels which find their way to Detroit and Buffalo would-, if a suitable breakwater were provided, discharge their cargoes at Goderich. The depth of water is greater at Goderich than it is at the Lime Kiln crossing.
What is the depth ?
In the neighbourhood of 21 feet.
Is that a natural harbour ?

Yes, certainly. Strong representations have been made to the government in the interest of this breakwater. As a matter of fact the delegation asked for a much larger breakwater than is being provided. but it is expected that this one, built as an experiment, will demonstrate its utility and warrant its -extension later on.
How is this breakwater toi be built-on solid masonry?
My intention was, if found practicable, to advise the building of this breakwater with concrete.

I have a very kindly feeling for the town of Goderich, and if the hon. minister is acting on the advice of his engineers I think it will be money well spent. There has been a great deal of difficulty in the past in regard to the piers constructed there, but as the hon. gentleman (Mr. Holmes) says, perhaps, they were not constructed in th-e right way. They did not run at the right angle out into the lake. If the hon. minister has reliable information as to the practicability of making a harbour there, I believe it ought to be a good harbour of refuge and if it is found that vessels can make that harbour in any weather it will bring a great deal of business to that part of the province.
The hon. minister says he is going to make the breakwater of concrete. How deep below water level is he going to put the concrete ?
As a rule we just put it below the extreme water level.

If the breakwater is not put deep enough below the low water-level the waves will lift it. The hon. member for West Huron (Mr. Holmes) speaks of this being a great shipping port and says that grain is going this way. He evidently has given up his view in favour of the transcontinental railway and has gone in for the water route.
I think this will be- part of the transcontinental route because that line of railway already runs to Goderich.

I have had a lot of correspondence in reference to this work with people in Stratford, Mitchell and other places along the line and they are strongly in favour of something being done at Goderich. I am very strongly in favour of this vote.

I also have a v-ery kindly feeling for the old town of Goderich, because of the service that harbour renders to the country in the early days when we had no railways. I was horn within a short distance of the place and know something about it. I think it is a very wise expenditure of money which has for its object the making of Goderich a harbour of refuge. It is important that this work should be proceeded with when we consider the distance that vessels have to go up Lake Huron before finding a harbour of refuge. I may also say in reference to this- grant of $5,000 to Grand Bend, that I am pleased to see that the hon. minister has placed in the -estimates a sum for the construction of a breakwater at that place. I was up there

a few days ago and there are some people who are very sceptical about this item being spent. I hope the hon. minister will not disappoint them this time. An item was placed in the estimates upon a former occasion and just before the general election an engineer was sent up to make some surveys. I am not going to say that the surveys were so effective that they brought about the state of affairs that existed at the last election, but I will say that in the end of the township in which the work was proposed to be undertaken, every vote was polled for the government candidate against the hon. member for East Lambton (Mr. Simmons). Even some of the hon. gentleman's own friends are very sceptical to-day about that work. I am very pleased to find this estimate here, and I hope the hon. minister will not disappoint them and will let the contract for the work at once. This place is very much in need of a breakwater. We have heard a good deal to-night of the fishermen of different parts of the country but I think this is one of the best fishing poihts, if not the best fishing point, on the Take Huron shore. The fishermen have no place to land their boats and there have been great complaints in the past from them. In addition Grand Bend is becoming very popular as a summer resort. Many people from different parts of Ontario go there (o camp. The hon. member for South Huron (Mr. McEwan) knows something about this as do other hon. members. I think the hon. member for North Perth (Mr. McLaren) and the hon. member for London (Mr. Hyman) will bear me out in what I say. A great many people come from London and spend the summer in cottages (here. We have spent about $20,000 at this place. While I was in the municipal council we had some dredging work done at the mouth of the Au Sable river and it does seem to be a natural harbour. I think $22,000 would be a sufficient expenditure to construct a work that would be a credit to the government and a relief to the people of Grand Bend.

I want to suggest to the hon. Minister of Public Works that if money is expended well everybody is gratified and if it is lost everybody is discouraged. We had some experience in building'a bridge over (he Shubenacadie river some two or three years ago. Some American engineers came up there who were not acquainted with the Bay of Fundy tide. They said it was folly to go down to bedrock and they put their piers on the hard-pan without reaching the rock. The tides came in and every one of the piers were moved. They had to go down and reach bedrock and the work was then made permanent. If you are going to make a good wharf you should go down to bedrock and if you do anything else you will find that it will be a failure.

We are all interested in this work on ac-Mr. SHERRITT.
count of the representations that have been made by the shipping and commercial interests of the province. As to the work itself it is probably to some extent an experiment as to what the results will be. I am confident from the representations made to me by practical men, captains of the large boats and others, (Jiat it will certainly bring many millions of bushels of grain to the Huron shore that now go to the American side. The trade of the whole Dominion will be very large if we are successful in establishing a good harbour of refuge at Goderich.
Gore's landing-wharf, $3,000.
May I ask the hon. minister, if, in regard to this item and also in regard to the next item of $4,000 for the Honora wharf, these amounts will complete the works ?
The total cost of the first one ife estimated by the chief engineer to be $3,000. The Honora wharf work will cost $7,000 to complete.

Since the Liberals came into power these docks have been strung out all along the shore of the Algoma district. There were private wharfs there before, built by the enterprise of individuals, and fees were charged on the shipping, but the government entered into the business, and rendered useless the expenditure by private citizens on these wharfs. Is it proposed to charge rent for the use of these docks ?
Yes.
You built a dock at Bruce Mines which cost $12,000, and last year you realized the paltry sum of $10.
There is a growing business in that district.

Yes, and there is a growing business in the city of Toronto, and vessels have to pay for the use of the docks there. It is all on a par with the building of docks at Hawkestone in East Simcoe, against which I protested. This government practically threw $3,000 into the lake for the purpose of getting a little political advantage, but it did not help them a bit, and that dock is rotting to-day.

I am not anxious to build any work without necessity.
Kingsville-filling superstructure of extension of breakwater with stone ballast, $4,000.
The estimated cost of this is $3,840. This work originally cost $15,000.
Is this for the west pier or the east pier ?
The west pier.
Was there not something the matter with one-of these piers ?

The chief engineer tells me that some damage was reported, but he does not consider it very dangerous.
Little Bear creek-dredging, $2,000.
This is in Kent county, and it is a very necessary work.
Is it between Chatham and the lake ?

The creek enters into the channel at the eastern side of St. Anne's island, Lake St. Clair, and is about ten miles from Chatham and seven from Wallaceburg.
Little Current-improvement of northern steamboat channel in Georgian bay, $15,000.

It is proposed to have a channel 200 feet wide and 21 feet deep at lowest water. If that work were carried out for the whole distance, it would cost between $150,000 and $200,000. Large shipowners, the Messrs. Long, among others, have reported that some considerable improvement can be made by a reasonable appropriation from time to time.
How much has already been expended on that channel.
The total expenditure up to January, 1903, was $83,000.
Is that channel at Little Current the only place between Manitoulin and the north shore where there is not 20 feet of water ?
That is the only place, so far as my information goes.

I should say that on the Canadian side of the St. Mary's river, there are not 20 feet of water in some places, and even if you do this work, you would still he obliged to use Hay lake channel for freighters.
The hon. gentleman is correct. I am informed by the chief engineer that in some places there is only 18 or 19 feet of water.
I do not think there are 16 feet in some parts of the old channel of the St. Mary's river, and we would have to complete all that work to make us independent of our neighbours.

There is no doubt that my hon. friend is right, but we will make this expenditure in the meantime.
Leamington-wharf, $3,800.

This is in Essex county, and the work is undertaken under the report of the engineer.
Midland harbour-improvements, $12,000.
I saw last week in the town of Midland a plan of a proposed dock there. Is that the plan that is to be followed-the one that was sent to the town clerk V
The chief engineer informs me that that is the plan on which tenders are being called for.

By way of explanation, let me state the position. Owing to the fact that docks were being built at a great many places, the town of Midland made this ' offer to the government of Canada. They said, we will purchase this water frontage for $10,000 and hand it over to the government on condition that the government will build a dock on it. That was agreed to, and on that understanding the town voted the $10,000, purchased the site, and handed it over to the government. By the plan which the department have sent to the town council it appears they have actually given a portion of this frontage to some party friends. I would ask the minister what consideration has been received by the government for this portion, on which these people have built a dock ?

If there is any foundation for the hon. gentleman's statement that the government have given away to party friends or to anybody else any portion of the property which the town conveyed to the government, it would be a matter for inquiry.
I asked whether it was given for nothing, or whether it was paid for V
It was not given at all. It was not either sold or given. The facts are not as the hon. gentleman states. ,	.

The plan shows that a part of this property which was purchased by the town and handed over to the department has to-day a dock built upon it by party friends of hon. gentlemen opposite. I can tell the minister that the effect of this action is such that had the question to buy the site and hand it over to the government to be put again before the town of Midland, it would be voted down almost unanimously. I do not know who is to blame for it, hut I suppose the Department of Marine and Fisheries. The little spur of dock which the town is getting to-day for the $10,000 which they gave is so trifling that I am sure if they had known what they were going to get they would never have

voted the money. May I ask what rent is being received by the department for the use of the storehouses which are on this property that the government acquired from the town ?

I may say that I have not looked into this matter personally, but either my hon. friend is greatly mistaken or the officials of my department are deceived. As the matter came up before, I asked them to look carefully into it, and they say that there is no foundation whatever for the statement, but that we have all the property that was handed over to us by the town. No rents have been received, and no action has been taken with regard to this property. The transfer was only completed a short time ago, and the plans have been prepared.
Do any of these parties who are in occupation of this government property pay any rent to the department V
The deputy minister informs me no.
Was not an application received by the minister from a firm in the town of Midland inquiring what rent was being asked by the department for this dock, and making an overture for renting ?
I will ask the deputy minister to make a memorandum of that. He says he has no recollection.

I can tell the minister that I saw the letter from his own department to those parties, acknowledging the receipt of their letter, and saying that the matter would be considered; but they heard nothing further.
Will the hon. gentleman give the name of the party V

Stafford & Company-the Midland Mercantile Company. They wanted to rent the warehouse, and were willing to pay $500 a year for it; but one of the hon. minister's party friends has it, presumably for nothing.
Not to my knowledge. My hon. friend knows that it is not in the plan or policy of the department to remove the old buildings.

I do not suppose the hon. gentleman will interfere with them. In fact, there is no room on the new docks to put any buildings. I can tell the minister that the handling of that dock has not been such as to win any friends to the government. One of their own party friends, Mr. Playfair, has possession of that dock without paying any rental. This1 is like some other actions of the government there. For

instance the Minister of Marine and Fisheries, at my solicitation, decided to put up two range lights. The department had the lights sent to the town, and what do you suppose they did ? Instead of placing them where they should have been placed, they decide, because Mr. Playfair had a couple of electric lights, to send them back to Ottawa or somewhere else; and in the meantime the marine trade has had to depend on two little lights which the people there supposed were fire-flies among the trees. I suppose the government think that Mr. Playfair can help them. All I can say is that I court his opposition, and I court the opposition of the government if they conduct other matters at Midland as they have done this. When parties were willing to pay a decent rent for the property if they had a chance at competition for it, these parties have had the use of the dock and the warehouses without paying a cent of remuneration. It will be news for the people, and from that they will judge how the general business of the country is carried on.
I think my hon. friend is mistaken, but I will have a further report made in regard to this matter.

It ought to be a simple matter to ascertain whether or not the land conveyed by the town of Midland to the crown is in part occupied by other persons, and I should think it would be advisable for my hon. friend the Minister of Public Works to bring the plan here and have some explanation of the matter placed before the House. I should think my hon. friend might bring the plan down to-morrow.

We will have a copy of the plan brought down to-morrow. I will have a report made on the other point, and if such a state of affairs exists as my hon. friend described, it is wholly without my knowledge. I am not aware, nor do I think that my deputy is, that any sucb state of affairs existed.
Pembroke-wharf, $10,000.
Permit me to ask the hon. minister if he intends to go on with the work at Little Bear Creek ? That has been in the estimates four or five years in succession and nothing done.

There is a dredge working in that locality, and I have given instructions to have it sent there at once.
Parry Sound-wharf, $8,000.
Where is that wharf to be located ?
It is to be built by the Parry Sound Lumber Company.
How much is the hon. minister giving the company for that dock ?
Nothing; the site is free.

You have a very fa-favourable proposition from the town of Parry Sound.
Point Edward-dredging, $6,000.
What is the extent of the work there ?

The work at that place is very important. Large boats could not get up to the wharf, and we are consequently having this work - done. I think that $6,000 will finish the work under contemplation at present.
Port Burwell-improvement of harbour (revote, $5,000), $34,000.

This will complete the work under contract there. This is for all the improvements going on there under the Department of Public Works, and the chief engineer informs me that it will complete it.
Port Stanley-dredging, $4,000.
Does this involve the replacing of the gentleman who died a short time ago and who superintended the works there ? Is it necessary to re-appoint another man to look after the dredges?
No, I do not think it is.
Then, there will be no appointment made ?

None.
Port Perry-dredging harbour, $2,200.
Is anything being done in connection with dredging the river leading up to Port Perry ?

Perhaps if we had a dredge there we might do it out of the general votes.
Port Perry-dredging harbour, $2,200.
This breakwater was built a number of years ago and badly wrecked. It should be lengthened very materially. In fact, a new one should be built further out.
I am making an effort to improve the one we have.
Has the dredging which was going on last year been finished, and what are the results ?

It is not finished, but the work done this season has given great satisfaction.
Rosedale-wharf, $1,000.

This is a very necessary work, and I might point out in connection with that water-way now in the ,	415
control of the Dominion government that there is a number of logs towed and brought through the locks from time to time, occasionally some fall out of the boom or crib and become water-logged and are a perfect nuisance. From time to time we expend money to clear these out of the channel. Logs 12 to 16 feet are sunk in ten feet of water, boats strike them, the screws and paddle wheels become broken and other injuries and accidents occur. The province has control of these logs, but inasmuch as the government has taken over these waterways, it should look into the matter and see if the Department of Public Works or the Department of Railways and Canals has not authority to have those logs taken away. That is to give any one finding a log in the water a right to take it as his own property. I can assure the minister that in that way the government would save a good deal of money, many accidents would be avoided and the channels and water courses would be cleared of logs. Another point is that the locks of all the systems operate' very slowly. The gates should be changed and should be made to operate much more rapidly than they do. Then, too, a great deal of country in the northern half of Victoria and Haliburton, near the Trent river, could be thrown open to traffic by the construction of four locks opening from the water north of Balsam lake into Haliburton. This would throw open a tract of country1 over 100 miles in length, containing much valuable birch and maple, which cannot now be hauled out to the railways owing to the conformation of the country. But I have previously entered into this detail and the plans and data are always in the departments.

1 will be pleased to have this matter looked into.
River Syden 1mm-improvement of, $5,800.
How is that money being expended ?

Principally in dredging. It is to improve the navigable channels of the Sydenham river. My hon. friend (Mr. Clancy) is familiar with these places. This is a work on which we made some representations. It is in the county of Bothwell, and this work is along the lines of representations made by a deputation introduced by the hon. gentleman.
I suppose this money is to be expended in the east branch of the river.
I am not sufficiently familiar with the river to say.

I call the attention of the hon. minister to this matter, because the River Svdenliam includes the north and east branches. Wallaceburg is at the junction of the north and east branches, and I sup-



pose this is to be expended between Wallace-hurg and Dresden.
This is to carry out the work asked for by the deputation introduced by the hon. gentleman.
As that is a very pressing work, particularly at this time of the year, I would ask if it would not be possible to send a dredge in there at once ?
I will give instruction to the engineer to have it taken up at once.
There is a good dredge at his disposal, it is a very important work, and if some portion of it could be done during the present season it would be of great advantage to the people there.

During the last two sessions I drew the attention of the government to some work that was very necessary in the harbour of Port Credit, .on Lake Ontario. Will the hon. minister state what is going to be done about that ?

The hon. gentleman brought it to my attention, and I sent for a report. One of the great difficulties is that the harbour there is private property, and whatever may have been the policy of the department in the past, it is not now the policy of the department, except under exceptional circumstances, to spend public money on property which is not the property of the Crown. I Intended to write my hon. friend about that in order that he might take it up.

Although that is the policy of the government, I do not think it has always been adhered to. There are other instances in Ontario where harbours are in exactly the same position. This is very close to Toronto, where the kon. gentleman has a dredge working all the time, and perhaps the hon. minister could allow that dredge to go to Port Credit and dredge out some of the sand that is continually drifting in there.

I think no one would object to that, and I will see that it is attended to, if there is a dredge in that locality.
Ottawa river-improvement of narrows at Petewawa above Pembroke-to pay G. C. Pou-pore in full for work done previous to July 1, 1903 (revote of lapsed amount), $7,000.

This is an amount of $7,000 that has been voted for several years. The contractor filed claims for a larger amount. This was in the main estimates, and I had it struck out, in order to look into it. After discussion of the matter the contractor has agreed to accept this, and I am asking this in order to make the settlement.
River St. Lawrence-dredging steamboat channel through shoal at foot of Wolfe Island, $5,000.
I do not see anything in the main estimates for the Canadian channel through the Thousand Islands.
Is not this a part of it ?
I understand a survey was made with a view to running a channel there.
My hon. friend knows that we must have our new Ontario dredge before we can do that.

This work at the foot of Wolfe island is very useful.
Regulation of waters at Lake Simcoe and Couchiching-repairs to works at Washago, &c.. $2,000.
THE MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS. A great deal of damage is done at this place from the overflow of the water in consequence of the government works. I find that $7,652 have been spent there in time past, and representations have been made to me that this $2,000 will renew this work in such a way as to protect the people of that locality from further loss.

At certain times in the past there was an overflow by the water of Lake Simcoe backing up on the south side. But since the stop-logs have been put in a few years ago, I understand no further trouble lias been felt. I do not know what this $2,000 is needed for, unless it is to make a more perfect arrangement.
This is for repairs to those works, to those stop-logs.
I have always understood that the people of Orillia township were satisfied with the arrangement.

There is a report in the Department of Railways and Canals showing that in certain seasons of the year the water rises on all these lakes, but there is no more overflow in this locality than anywhere else. But on account of the blasting that was done years ago, these-stop-logs were put in. If the minister means that this money is to repair those stop-logs, that is all right ; but if it means that it is to reduce the present level of Lake Couchiching and Lake Simcoe, he will find the country will not tolerate it.
Sault Ste. Marie-harbour improvements, including dredging of approaches (revote), $18 -300.

I would like to have some explanation from the minister of what is proposed to he done here. I was up ait [DOT] Sault Ste. Marie recently, and it appears to

me a good deal of work needs to be done there.
Representations have been made to me that a good deal of work was required there, but I have had no money to do it with. With this money it may be possible to do some dredging this fall.

That is a place where I think the government will be wise in taking a comprehensive view of the matter, and in proceeding deliberately upoi. some careful system by which that river will be. utilized, and by which we may have a channel that will compare with the American channel. At present docks are being built through private enterprise. A dock was put up recently by a private company, who claim that they have spent a large amount of money. I do not speak with any technical knowledge, but it appears to me that that dock is carried out into the river too far.
I think the government would meet the wishes of the country if they proceeded in some comprehensive manner with their work on the water front, which is to serve as a dock along the Canadian Soo. There is no one who visits the American side and then comes across to the Canadian side, but must feel, if he is a patriotic Canadian, ashamed of the appearance of our own country, as compared with the American side. That remark applies particularly to the lack of dockage accommodation and to the slovenly condition in which the Canadian side generally appears. There is evidently an immense amount of shipping done there* and I should think that some such system as has been adopted at Montreal would be a proper system at the Soo, that is to say, that instead of running out these docks or piers into the river, we should have a dock extending along the line of the river parallel to the shore, to serve as a means of anchorage for all the vessels coming from the Canadian locks. There is another matter that deserves attention, and that is the condition of the land round about the Canadian locks. On the American side everything is in beautiful condition, there is a lawn and a park, but on the Canadian side everything is rough and unfinished. It is important that we should make our side compare favourably with the other side. Although I do not often advocate the expenditure of money, I think it is important that the Canadian side of the Soo should be considerably improved. The Canadian Soo has a great future before it, tlie trade through that channel is rapidly increasing, and the percentage of increase is now in favour of our locks. I think we would be justified in expending money on a well-considered plan, both as regards the dredging of the river and improving the land round about the locks. I might remind the hon. Minister of Public Works that the Americans are spending a very large sum of money almost every year, and 415}	'
there is a very large contemplated expenditure at the present time in improving their channel. When we are coming into direct competition with them, as we are at that point and at some other points on the lakes, I would be somewhat generous in the expenditure of money. Of course, I would advocate a very well-considered plan for the whole scheme before the expenditure is engaged in.

I think on this matter we are almost unanimous and the only reason I did not take it up sooner was that I wanted to have a plan prepared before I asked for my vote.
Thessalon-breakwater, $5,000.
What is that for ? You have a government dock there already that produces almost nothing in revenue.

This is to make provision towards the construction of a breakwater 420 feet long at Thessalon for the protection of all classes of vessels on the great lakes. Very strong representations have been made to me by people engaged in the vessel trade and by fishermen and others upon the subject and it has been pointed out to me that the wharf under present conditions' is of very little use to them. It will be a great advantage to the district to have another harbour of refuge there and I have brought down a vote for this purpose.
What depth of water is there ?
From twelve to fifteen feet of water.

I do not know whether the hon. minister has been at Thessalon, but he must know that this has been a town for fifteen years. It has done business for the last fifteen years and there is a very expensive government dock at that point now and as there is little or no revenue why this large expenditure should be gone into now seems incredible. I am sorry that the hon. member for Algoma (Mr. Dyment) is not here because I would like to compliment him personally on being able to get more money expended in his riding than the most sanguine well-wisher for the distribution of public funds with the view of political advantage coming from it.
Toronto harbour-works at eastern entrance, close piling, channel face of east pier and levelling up pier, $20,000.

I observe there is nothing in the estimates for the dredging out of Toronto harbour. This work has been necessitated because of the persistent refusal of the government of Canada for the last sixty years to take steps to protect what was once a peninsula inclosing the harbour of Toronto. I have the documents in my desk now but I do not want to weary the commit-

tee about it at this time. It is really incredible when we look over the official documents in connection with the preservation of Toronto harbour for the last sixty years to see how impossible it has been, because of changing governments and changing opinions, to have anything permanent done in respect to the preservation of the harbour. These eastern works have been made necessary because all the recommendations made again and again looking towards the protection of the peninsula have been entirely ignored. The force of the waves of Lake Ontario destroyed the peninsula and formed the present island. Since 1833, Capt. Bonny-eastle, who was then the harbour master, and his various successors ha ve been recommending that something should be done for the preservation of the harbour. Capt. Bonnyc-astle's statement were prophetic, and unless the government do something at an early day in regard to the diversion of the channel of the Don, and in the way of dredging, there will be good grounds for complaint.

I do not think we can take up the discussion at the present time of the improvements of the Don. Representations were made to me asi to dredging at the eastern entrance. I was unable to get a dredge to do this work. It was only last week that I was able to get a' dredge, the one that had been working for the city of Toronto and I gave the owners a contract. We happened to procure a dredge up the lakes but they got into some trouble and they were not able to fulfil their contract. As to the other work that will have to .be taken up again.
Toronto harbour-works at eastern entrance -to pay Magann and Phin in full and final settlement of all claims in connection with their contract of February 10, 1900, for the extension of the western pier, $9,100.51.
How has this adjustment been arrived at ?
This settlement was made with the officials of the department and on the report of our own officials.
Will the hon. minister bring the papers down in connection with this matter ?

Yes. I will be very glad to. I have not looked into them myself.
Victoria harbour-dredging, $4,000.
Will that money be spent this year and if so will it complete the dredging at that point ? This is an important point. This year 75,000,000 feet of lumber will be cut there.

This money will be all spent. There have been applications for about $3,000 of $4,000 Mr. CLARKE.
more to complete this work, but I do not think we can take it upi this year.
Wiarton-wharf, $10,000.
This is for a new wharf at Wiarton.
What will be the total cost ?	'

The total cost will be about $11,000. My hon. friend is familiar with the conditions there. Owing to the establishment of new factories at that place strong representations have been made as to the necessity for this work.
Who furnishes the site ?

The site does not cost us anything, but the chief engineer tells me that he expects that will be given. I do not know whether it will be furnished by the provincial government or by the town, but at any rate it will be furnished.
Some resolutions reported.
The MINISTER OF FINANCE moved the adjournment of the House.

Mr. Speaker, before the House adjourns, I wish to refer to a matter that I understand was brought before the Committee of Supply last evening. The hon. member for East Simcoe (Mr. Bennett), I understand, intimated to the committee that I was an interested party in a company at Newmarket which was in receipt of government work. I wish to say that the statement is wholly without foundation.
I know nothing about the company's financial arrangements and I have never had any interest in it. I do not know whether it has shareholders or whether it has not. It is quite true that I have felt it to be my duty from time to time to endeavour to promote the interests of this company. It is carrying on business in a town I am interested in and for many reasons I wish that town well. I am pleased to be able to be of service to that town in promoting the welfare of a great industry like the Office Specialty Company. Further than taking a public interest in the matter, I know nothing in respect to it. I think it would have been fairer if the hon. gentleman had reserved his remarks till I could have been in the House so that my denial might have immediately followed his insinuation.
speakername: The POSTMASTER GENERAL (Hon. Sir William Mulock).

speechtext:
I happened to be in the town of Newmarket during the by-election, last spring, and I heard a wordy altercation between two electors. One was pretending that the Postmaster General was the backbone of the town of Newmarket, and in support of his contention he announced that

the Postmaster General was a stockholder In this company. Tile other contended that the Postmaster General was not interested in it, and that if the town had to depend on the Postmaster General, the office specialty works would not have been there. The Postmaster General's supporter repeated time and again that the Postmaster General was interested in this work, and the other gentleman, who was a Conservative, I need hardly say, asserted time and again that the town had not to thank the Postmaster General for this enterprising establishment. It now seems that this gentleman was right. This gentleman also asserted that the Postmaster General was never known to enter into any enterprise in the town. Be that as it may, since the Postmaster General says that he is not interested, I can only regret that he has not joined with other enterprising men in this concern, which is so creditable to the town of Newmarket. I hope the Postmaster General will follow at an early date, the example set by other gentlemen who have invested money in manufacturing concerns in that town.

The point of my observation was to deny the insinuation of the member for East Simcoe, that I had been-as he put it-sending grist to my mill, and using my position as a minister to enrich myself through the medium of this company. That was an unfair insinuation to make on the floor of this House. It is false in every respect.

It was the assertion of one of the Postmaster General's political friends, that his enterprise was so great, and that such was his admiration for the town of Newmarket, that he had been one of the gentlemen who had engaged in this enterprise. However, that appears to be untrue, and I join in wishing well to Newmarket.

I regret to have to state that I received a telegram from Springhill this morning stating that a very serious explosion has occurred in the Dominion public building there, by which a gentleman named McDowell was killed, and a gentleman named Eaton and two boys seriously injured. I have received a later telegram saving that probably Mr. Eaton will die. I aslt the Minister of Public Works to make an immediate investigation into the cause of this frightful accident, which has resulted in loss Qf life, and has wrecked the public building which has just been constructed in that town.
What fuel were they using ?
Nova Scotia coal, I think.
I was told this morning that I would receive an answer later in the day as to the report of Tread-gold Commission, and the printing of the evidence.
I spoke to the Premier and lie intended to give an answer, but I may say that tlie report has not been received yet.
I would ask whether the Bill to amend the Audit Act is to be proceeded with, and if so, whether any date has been fixed for its consideration?
I am unable to fix any date with regard to that Bill at present.
The hon. gentleman does intend to proceed with it this session ?
I have not given It consideration of late. I am not able to say anything more definite on that point than that the matter is still nnder consideration.
What business may we expect to-morrow ?
Continuation of supplies.
Motion agreed to, and House adjourned at 12.40 a.no.
Wednesday, October 7, 1903.
